fields.why: Six NCHS urban-rural categories are compared by t-tests against noncore, and age, education and race/ethnicity groups are shown with values per group in Tables 1-2.

Rurality (6 levels), age (3 groups, 'higher in older age groups'), education (4 levels, 'adults with less education') and race/ethnicity (8 groups, tabulated) all carry an outcome per group; sex and disability are binary.
The only stated test is t-tests 'with the most rural (noncore) category as the reference group' (per-group vs referent); age, education and race groups have no test across them, so side by side.

brief_issues: Whether a race/ethnicity breakdown shown only in a table, with no claim in the text, should get a side-by-side entry is left to 'record anything that looks groupwise'; A's inclusion is defensible. Employment status (5 levels, SES) could have been a separate side-by-side entry but adds no new dimension.
